data.what: The Moon's heights (LDEM_16, LDEM_128, LDEM_64 and the 80 m south polar DEM LDEM_80S_80M), cut into one global grid and three windows; and Shackleton's year of sunlight, worked out from them by tools/bake-lola.mjs
data.credit: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, LOLA laser altimeter (NASA/GSFC; the LOLA science team). Gridded data records from the NASA Planetary Data System.
data.changes: pooled to 1 pixel per degree (global) and cropped to three windows of 48 to 120 km; heights rounded to 4 to 32 m; the sunlight map is derived, not NASA's

data.what: The Moon's brightness (maria, highlands, bright rays)
data.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center/Arizona State University: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Wide Angle Camera global mosaic, as published in NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (CGI Moon Kit, SVS 4720)
data.changes: converted to grey and reduced to 360 x 180

data.credit: NASA Earth Observatory: Blue Marble Next Generation (Reto Stockli, NASA Earth Observatory, based on data from NASA MODIS)

data.what: The Moon's size, mass, gravity, day and orbit
data.credit: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive, Moon Fact Sheet (fetched 2026-10-03); orbit elements after Jean Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms
data.licence: facts are not copyrightable; credited as a courtesy

data.what: Earth's heights and sea floor (the whole globe at half a degree) and the coast, rivers and shelf round Cape Canaveral at 200 m
data.credit: AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (Terrarium), a composite of NASA SRTM, GEBCO (General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans), NOAA ETOPO1 and other public elevation sources
data.licence: open data: public-domain and open government sources; credited as a courtesy (see the registry page for each source's terms)
data.changes: zoom 3 averaged to 0.5 degree (deep sea stored 25 m coarse) and zoom 10 resampled to 0.002 degree over a 0.8 degree window; a biome map (green, desert, snow) derived from the Blue Marble picture is baked beside it

data.what: Earth seen from the sky and from space (the globe picture)
data.credit: NASA Earth Observatory: Blue Marble Next Generation with topography and bathymetry (Reto Stockli, NASA Earth Observatory, based on data from NASA MODIS), July 2004

data.what: Earth's size, mass, gravity, day, tilt and orbit
data.credit: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive, Earth Fact Sheet; orbit elements from JPL (E. M. Standish, Keplerian Elements for Approximate Positions of the Major Planets)
